title: MicroservicePrd:TenantRbac

_meta.purpose: Tenant/RBAC control microservice PRD for entitlement-to-scope packaging, tenant workload admission, and policy evidence across flat clean-architecture microservices. It packages services by tenancy and RBAC without creating product-grouping wrappers.

identity.ops_surface: managed through OpenTofu-owned infrastructure, root Makefile bootstrap/install/plan/apply targets, and oya ops surfaces; no manual SSH troubleshooting path

user_decisions: 2026-05-28:flat microservices are packaged later by tenancy and RBAC
2026-05-28:messenger, community, and mail are independent services; no umbrella grouping module exists
2026-05-28:messenger and mail must preserve strict personal/professional-life separation
2026-05-28:public customer URLs use oyatie.com while .dev remains internal/developer-only

responsibilities: resolve tenant entitlements into RBAC scopes
validate tenant workload admission without bypassing owning microservice policy
emit audit-chain evidence for entitlement and scope decisions
hold cloud-readiness evidence for tenant isolation, resource quota, workload identity, and service-account boundaries
keep clean-architecture boundaries explicit across domain, application, API, runtime, infrastructure, kernel, and library layers
non_goals: owning mail, messenger, community, calendar, HR, payroll, accounting, or healthcare domain data
creating product grouping wrappers, bundles, vertical grouping services, or market-label ownership boundaries
granting access without downstream microservice RBAC and tenant-policy evaluation
merging personal and professional life contexts for messenger or mail

acceptance_criteria.given: a tenant package resolves to enabled service surfaces
acceptance_criteria.when: a user requests a microservice capability
acceptance_criteria.then: the decision carries tenant_id, entitlement_set_id, role binding, policy scope, and audit evidence refs before the owning microservice evaluates access

acceptance_criteria.given: a regulated tenant enables healthcare-related capabilities
acceptance_criteria.when: healthcare-integration or adjacent services are exposed
acceptance_criteria.then: the exposure is controlled by regulatory pack, tenancy, and RBAC scopes rather than a market-label product boundary

acceptance_criteria.given: messenger or mail is enabled for both personal and professional contexts
acceptance_criteria.then: personal and professional life scopes remain separate in policy, evidence, and downstream service evaluation

preview: packaging-axis evidence for tenancy and RBAC
stable: regional and regulatory pack activation evidence
GA: hyperscaler-grade operational SLOs for policy decisions

out_of_scope.why: flat microservices are packaged later by tenancy/RBAC entitlement
mail, messenger, community, and other microservices own their domain data

out_of_scope.item: context collapse across personal and professional life
out_of_scope.why: mail and messenger require strict separation

data_model.retention: audit-chain evidence retained per tenant compliance pack; operational cache TTLs are bounded and non-authoritative

targets.preview: all scope decisions carry evidence refs

goals.scalability: policy decisions cache by tenant/scope while preserving service-owned authorization evaluation
goals.security: fail closed on missing tenant, entitlement, role, context, or audit evidence
goals.performance: p99 scope decisions remain below interactive service admission budgets
goals.efficiency: reuse canonical tenant/RBAC packaging axes instead of market-label wrappers
goals.reliability: policy evidence is deterministic, replayable, and audit-chain linkable

risks.risk: policy overreach into service domain logic
risks.mitigation: tenant-rbac produces scope decisions; owning services still evaluate domain policy

risks.risk: context collapse between personal and professional life
risks.mitigation: explicit context_model and planning-closure success rule preserve separation
retired grouping wording gates and planning-closure packaging-axis contract

competitive.lesson: role bindings are explicit and auditable
tenant isolation is a full-stack design concern, not a branding boundary
application authorization should be policy-decidable and testable

best_practices: audit evidence for every admission decision
patterns: tenant entitlement to RBAC scope mapping
anti_patterns: manual policy exceptions without audit evidence
service domain ownership inside tenant/RBAC packaging

decision_log.decision: Tenant/RBAC is the packaging axis for flat microservices, not a product grouping boundary.
Messenger and mail retain strict personal/professional context separation.
